access-token.access-token-deletion: Are you sure you want to delete access token `{{description}}`?
access-token.access-token-deletion-description: This action is irreversible. You will need to update any services using this token to use a new token.
access-token.create-first: Create your first REST API token
access-token.description: Create and revoke personal access tokens for REST API clients.
access-token.about-description: An app or script holding a personal access token (PAT) can act as your account until the token expires or you revoke it.
access-token.empty-description: A token lets a script or app call the API as you. It is shown once at creation, then listed here so you can revoke it.
access-token.guideline-shown-once: A token is shown only once, right after you create it (it is copied to your clipboard). Store it somewhere safe, like a password manager.
access-token.guideline-one-per-app: Create a separate token for each app or script, so you can revoke one without breaking the others.
access-token.guideline-expiration: Prefer tokens that expire. Long-lived tokens are a bigger risk if they leak.
access-token.guideline-review: Check the last-used time from time to time, and delete tokens you no longer recognize or need.
access-token.label: MCP & API
access-token.title: REST API access tokens
access-token.integration-description: Manage MCP connections and personal access tokens for your notes.
access-token.mcp-description: Choose Streamable HTTP in Codex and enter this URL. Leave the Bearer token environment variable blank. Under HTTP headers, add Authorization and paste the full Bearer value shown when you create the connection.
access-token.api-description: To read and write notes through the REST API, replace <YOUR_PAT> with a personal access token. Requests follow your account's note permissions.
access-token.copy-failed: Could not copy. Select and copy the text manually.
access-token.web-clipper-title: Use a token with Memos Web Clipper

mcp-connection.title: MCP connections
mcp-connection.description: Create an MCP token for Codex or another client. The token works immediately and shares its validity period with connections using it.

mcp-connection.create-error: Could not create the connection. Try again.
mcp-connection.token-shown-once: The token appears only once. In Codex headers, enter Authorization as the key and paste the full value below, including Bearer.
mcp-connection.unsupported: This instance does not offer MCP connection tokens.
mcp-connection.delete-description: Deleting this token immediately blocks further requests that use it.
mcp-connection.delete-error: Could not delete the token. Try again.

memo-export.description: Move your memos and attachments between Memos instances with a single ZIP file.
memo-export.export-description: Download every memo you created, including comments, archived memos, and attachment files, in Memos Export Format.
memo-export.export-detail: A ZIP file with one Markdown file and one JSON record per memo.
memo-export.import-description: Import a Memos export file from this or another Memos instance. Memos keep their identifiers, so importing the same file twice does not create duplicates.
memo-export.import-detail: Select a ZIP file exported by Memos.
memo-export.label: Export & Import
memo-export.policy-duplicate-description: Keep the existing memos and add the imported versions as new memos.
memo-export.policy-question: {{count}} of these memos already exist in your account. What should happen to them?
memo-export.policy-replace-description: Overwrite their content and settings with the imported version.
memo-export.policy-skip-description: Leave the existing memos as they are.
memo-export.export-busy: Another export is running. Try again in a moment.

preference.appearance-description: Choose how the app looks and which language it uses for your account.

preference.double-click-edit-description: Open your own memos in the editor by double-clicking them.
preference.label: Preferences
preference.language-description: Updates the interface language immediately and saves it to your account.
preference.link-preview-description: Show a preview card under bare links wherever memos are displayed.
preference.save-media-metadata-description: For future uploads, save available camera, capture time, location, image dimensions, and basic video details. Anyone who can view the attachment can receive this metadata. Existing attachments are unchanged.
preference.theme-description: Applies the selected theme immediately on this device.
preference.uploads-privacy-description: Control privacy-sensitive information submitted with uploaded media.

editor.label: Editor
editor.markdown-mode-description: Write and edit memos as Markdown text instead of formatted text.

memo-view.delete-confirm: Are you sure you want to delete view `{{title}}`?
memo-view.page-description: Create reusable views with fields, operators, time helpers, and tag matching. Use examples as starting points, then validate before saving.
memo-view.form-description: Name the view and define the memo filter expression it should apply.
memo-view.filter-help: Combine expressions with {{and}}, {{or}}, and {{not}}. Time fields are timestamps — use {{now}}, {{duration}}, {{timestamp}}, and accessors like {{year}}. Tags support {{sets}}, and {{size}} measures length.
memo-view.empty-description: Save a filter to quickly return to the memos you need.
memo-view.title-filter-required: Title and filter cannot be empty

storage.accesskey-description: Access key ID for the bucket or S3-compatible service.
storage.bucket-description: Bucket where new attachment objects will be stored.
storage.current-storage-description: Choose where new attachments are stored. Existing attachments remain in their current storage location.
storage.database-description: Store attachment blobs directly in the application database.
storage.database-note-backup: Simple to back up together with notes on small instances.
storage.database-note-size: The database can grow quickly with many or large attachments.
storage.endpoint-description: Service endpoint, such as an AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, or other compatible URL.
storage.filepath-template-description: Used by local and S3 storage. Supports {timestamp}, {uuid}, and {filename}. Default: assets/{timestamp}_{uuid}_{filename}.
storage.insecure-skip-tls-verify-description: Disable TLS certificate verification for the S3 endpoint. Enable only for trusted endpoints using a self-signed certificate; this removes protection against man-in-the-middle attacks.
storage.label: Storage
storage.local-description: Store new attachments on the server file system. This is the default for new instances.
storage.local-note-backup: Persist and back up the attachment directory, especially in Docker or container deployments.
storage.local-note-path: Relative paths are written under the instance profile data directory.
storage.region-description: Region required by the provider. For some compatible services, any provider-accepted region string is enough.
storage.s3-configuration-description: Configure an S3-compatible bucket for new attachments.
storage.s3-description: Store new attachments in an S3-compatible object storage service.
storage.s3-note-config: Requires a valid endpoint, region, bucket, credentials, permissions, and server network access.
storage.s3-note-scale: Best for large attachment libraries, cloud deployments, or multiple application instances.
storage.secretkey-description: Secret access key for the bucket or S3-compatible service.
storage.secretkey-preserve-description: Leave blank to keep the existing secret key.
storage.use-path-style-description: Enable this for providers such as MinIO or some S3-compatible services that do not support virtual-hosted-style buckets.

welcome.title: Welcome to Memos

welcome.intro-write: A single sentence can be a whole memo.
welcome.intro-keep: Each memo stays with the day you wrote it.
welcome.intro-share: Sign in to access the notes you create.
welcome.write-sub: A single sentence can be a whole memo.
welcome.no-title-text: A memo starts with the thought itself. There is no title to fill in.
welcome.markdown-text: Markdown gives your words structure when you want it.
welcome.attach-text: Images, files, audio and a place come in through ＋.
welcome.keep-sub: Each memo stays with the day you wrote it.
welcome.calendar-text: Pick a day in the sidebar to see notes for that date.
welcome.tags-text: A word after # becomes a tag you can use to filter notes.
welcome.views-text: A custom view saves a filter.
welcome.share-sub: Organize topics in Spaces and add follow-up thoughts to your notes.
welcome.spaces-text: Organize notes by topic in Spaces.
welcome.comments-text: Add follow-up thoughts and updates to a note.
